title: Leadership Lesson 3: Integrity Matters
coreMove: Keep the stated principle intact at the first costly exception where everyone is watching.
sourcePressure: Defines integrity as coherence under pressure: principles remain real in costly cases or the culture learns that exceptions and excuses outrank standards.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating integrity as private sincerity, reputation, or honesty in easy cases.

counterintuition: numbers versus people as a flat binary

exampleSpecs.audience: clinic manager with a favored doctor request
exampleSpecs.stakes: integrity is tested when bending rules would be convenient
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she denies the off-log sample request and records it while the doctor waits
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sample cabinet key beside a logbook

exampleSpecs.audience: jury chair facing pressure for a sponsor film
exampleSpecs.stakes: principles must hold when money is in the room
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair reads the scoring rule before sponsor names are discussed
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a ballot stack beside a sponsor placard

exampleSpecs.audience: site supervisor tempted to skip wind limit
exampleSpecs.stakes: coherence matters when delay is expensive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he locks the crane controls after the wind meter crosses the stated limit
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wind meter clipped to a control box

exampleSpecs.stakes: exception for a wealthy family teaches cynicism
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she compares the advertised standard with the altered evaluation grid and reverses the admission
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an evaluation grid under an embossed folder

exampleSpecs.audience: choir director reviewing friend's weak audition
exampleSpecs.stakes: friendship tests the rule everyone heard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks the panel to predict member reaction if the exception leaks, then follows the rubric
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tuning fork beside an audition rubric

exampleSpecs.audience: landlord choosing whether to cite own unit
exampleSpecs.stakes: standards split if authority exempts itself
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he writes the same violation notice for his unit before delivering others
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a smoke alarm battery beside an inspection form

skillTargets: evaluate trust damage from convenient inconsistency

tryThisNowSpec: Find one standard you believe in and write the exception that will tempt you to bend it this month.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter
